title: 10 Signs You Have Survivor's Intelligence (The Rarest Kind of Smart)
description:
10 Signs You Have Survivor's Intelligence (The Rarest Kind of Smart)


This video breaks down survivor's intelligence, also called adaptive intelligence, using the 2022 "hidden talents" framework from Bruce Ellis, Ann Masten, Robert Sternberg, Nim Tottenham, and Willem Frankenhuis, along with a 2015 University of Minnesota study by Chiraag Mittal and Vladas Griskevicius showing how unpredictable childhoods build faster mental shifting, and Seth Pollak's research on threat perception in children raised around volatility. Ten signs are covered: reading a room instantly, moving on from dead plans without grieving them, getting calmer as things get worse, anticipating what people need, stretching very little very far, a memory built around warning value, distrust of things that come easily, learning fastest under real pressure, shifting between different versions of yourself, and always knowing where the exit is. Then three principles for an intelligence built for storms that's gone unemployed in calm weather.

If you've ever felt sharp in a crisis and strangely useless on a quiet Sunday, this one's for you.

Which of the ten signs hit you the hardest? Tell me in the comments.

#psychology #survivorsintelligence #adaptiveintelligence #childhoodtrauma #resilience #selfawareness #psychtoons

---

Research referenced

- Bruce Ellis, Ann Masten, Robert Sternberg, Nim Tottenham, Willem Frankenhuis (2022, *Development and Psychopathology*) — the "hidden talents" framework, stress-adapted skills as a genuine form of intelligence
- Chiraag Mittal & Vladas Griskevicius (2015, *Journal of Personality and Social Psychology*, University of Minnesota) — unpredictable childhoods and the inhibition/shifting trade-off
- Seth Pollak — children raised around volatility detecting anger from degraded facial cues faster than peers
- Ann Masten — "ordinary magic," resilience as normal developmental machinery under abnormal conditions
